_about: The Story page's two PATHS, one per project format (a feature and a short film are not the same road, and the page never mixes them). Since 19 Oct 2026 (owner) both are FOUR steps: Idea (the idea and the logline) · Characters & world (the Story Bible's cards) · Beat Sheet (the beat sheet choice, the step outline under its beats with an Unassigned bin, the lock and Send to screenplay; Setups & payoffs, Timeline and the free-text outline sit in closed boxes inside it) · Synopsis (the synopsis, tagged, beside the beats and pacing curve; ladder rungs 2-4 in a closed Treatment box). The Screenplay Writer is the next STAGE, reached by a button, not a step. Read by src/lib/story.js (PATH, pathProgress, hash mapping), src/pages/story.js (which draws every step on the page, in this order) and src/ui/stage-guide.js (which leaves out of the Story Guide every blueprint step a path step already asks). Nothing here is stored. A step is { id, sym, group, label, n, absorbs }; `sym` is its Material Symbols mark, read by the page's menu and by the rail's Story flyout (src/lib/navmodel.js moduleSections). `group` is the heading the step sits under in the section menu ('' draws none; the Pitch deck follows under a Tools heading only when the console switches it on). `n` is the step's STABLE NUMBER for old #path-N links — never renumber one and never reuse a retired one: 1 idea, 4 outline, 5 synopsis and 7 bible are live; 2 logline, 3 structure, 6 screenplay, 8 setups, 9 timeline, 10 lock, 11 character, 12 world and 13 conflict were steps once and now land through `aliases`. `aliases` maps, per format, every retired step id and number to the step that holds it now, so an old link (#path-6, #path-lock, #path-conflict, #pacing) lands on its new home and never falls back to the first step; scripts/test-story.mjs asserts every one. `absorbs` lists the blueprint questions the step asks INLINE, so each question is on the page once: "<ns>:<step id>" is the whole step; "<ns>:<step id>#rest" is the step WITHOUT its questions (its formula, craft, examples, relationship map and 'before moving on' checklist stay) because the Story Bible's own cards — see `cards` — ask them; "<ns>:treatment-ladder#<key>" is one rung of the ladder. `cards` names the Story Bible cards a step shows (src/data/story-bible.json). Every data-key of the blueprint steps that sit in the Story stage must be reachable here or in the Guide's cover (the cover sheet stays hidden on story.html and is edited on the project dashboard's Title page, through the same keys); scripts/test-stage-guide.mjs asserts it.
